name: Paula Hixon
languages: French (four years of it at Moravian College)
Spanish (from the copy desk, mostly obituaries)
equipment: Heavy coat: a corduroy car coat with a fake-fur collar
Pocket revolver: her father's .32, a retired Allentown patrolman's off-duty gun, which he made her promise to carry
Instant camera: a Polaroid SX-70 with three packs of film (30 pictures)
A 35mm Pentax with a flash and two rolls of Tri-X, for the paper
Notebook and pencil, and a box of Bic pens
A press card: THE POCONO LEDGER, STROUDSBURG — STAFF
A list of telephone numbers: her editor, the Stroudsburg State Police barracks, Ridgeview's public relations man
Newspaper: Thursday's Ledger, with her byline on a zoning board story
Car: a 1968 Volkswagen Beetle, orange, with a heater that does not work
features: Seen It in a Book (Educated origin: once per long rest she recalls one useful fact about history, science, law, geography or a book without a check; advantage on Research checks in a library, archive or registry; she reads old handwriting and legal language without a check)

There's an Explanation (Skeptic: once per short rest, when she fails a fear check, she names a rational cause aloud, in character, and the failure becomes a success and she gains no Dread; if her explanation happens to be true, the GM tells her so; advantage on Investigation checks to find the mechanism behind a thing that is not supernatural, and after 10 minutes searching a room the GM tells her whether any part of what is happening in it is a person's doing)

Careful Notes (Skeptic: once per short rest, after 10 minutes examining a scene, she asks the GM 'What here has been moved?', 'Who was here most recently: a person, an animal or something else?' or 'What here does not fit?' and gets a true answer; it never names a creature's rule outright)

Calm Explanation (Skeptic, 2nd level: once per long rest, as an action, she explains a frightening phenomenon to allies who can hear her; until the end of the scene they have advantage on fear checks against that one phenomenon)

Discipline: Scientist (Skeptic, 3rd level: during a long rest she can rig an apparatus, a Polaroid on a timer and a tripwire, a thread across a door, a thermometer on a string, and the GM tells her honestly what it records; advantage on Mechanics checks with instruments and cameras)

The Morgue and the Wire (Reporter background: she can get into any newspaper's back files and its staff will help; she reads a court docket, a coroner's report and a police blotter; in any town with a paper she can find the person who knows the gossip)

personality.traits: I take a picture of everything, because the picture remembers when I don't. I ask the second question. I am rude to people with power and very gentle with people without it.
personality.ideals: If it is not on paper, it did not happen. If it is on paper, somebody has to be able to check it.
personality.bonds: My father, a retired patrolman in Allentown, who reads every word I write. My mother, who came to Pinecrest for a week in 1948 when she was a typist and talked about it all my life.
personality.flaws: I can explain anything. When I can't, I take a picture of it instead of looking at it.

appearance: Twenty-nine, a short dark pixie cut, big tortoiseshell glasses, a corduroy car coat, a Polaroid on a strap round her neck and a Pentax round her shoulder.
backstory: Paula Hixon has been a reporter at the Pocono Ledger, a Stroudsburg weekly, for five years: zoning boards, school-board budgets, fires, the occasional bear. She went to Moravian College in Bethlehem on a scholarship and meant to go to New York, and her father had a stroke, and she stayed. Her editor wants a feature for the Sunday section, THE LAST SUMMER AT THE LAST GROWN-UPS' CAMP, with pictures: the old staff, the lake, Lantern Night. Paula wanted it for her mother, who spent a week at Pinecrest in July 1948 as a twenty-year-old typist from Allentown and kept the Lantern Night mask photograph on her dresser until she died. She brought three packs of Polaroid film and two rolls of Tri-X. The Polaroid is a new SX-70 she bought herself, and she is very proud of it. (Hook: the story. Her camera is the party's best instrument against Old Glass, and she should be the one who first sees a face that is not there.)
